top_choice_rationale: P001 credits targeted protein degradation as one achievement: a bifunctional molecule forms a ternary complex whose cooperativity is measurable and tunable, converting binding into removal of the target, a different mechanism from inhibition. It has been reproduced across many ligases and laboratories and reaches targets without a classical pocket, which is the generative potential I look for. Crews and Deshaies hold the 2001 concept and first demonstration, and Ciulli supplied the VHL ligand chemistry and structural and cooperativity account that made it a rational design discipline. The cereblon glue strand is a partly separate history and the citation should say heterobifunctional degraders. Clinical approval is still pending, which I treat as a timing risk and not a scientific defect. P003 is my mature, cleanly attributed fallback. P002 ranks below it because it drops Ciulli and splits the prize across two achievements, and base editing sits close to the 2020 prize. No award ranks last because several proposals are scientifically sound.
